clue.text: Among the rest, I am put back on

indicators.note: the words for 'I am' sit among the letters of the word for rest

parts.note: repose means rest
I am contracts to I'm

explanation.surface: A rider is told to restore something among the remaining items, ending on a teasing ellipsis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Among' puts IM inside REPOSE. The ellipsis carries 'put back on' into 5-across, where the same words do a different job.
explanation.definitionFit: To reimpose a rule or tax is to bring it into force again, to put it back on.

clue.text: Plant disease besets Kent apple

indicators.note: besets means surrounds, so the disease word wraps round the letters for Kent

parts.note: rust is a fungal disease of plants
Kent is a county in South-East England, abbreviated SE

explanation.surface: A fungal blight attacks a fruit grown in Kent, the Garden of England.
explanation.walkthrough: Kent is an English county in the South-East region, hence SE.
explanation.definitionFit: A russet is a variety of eating apple with a rough brownish skin.

clue.text: Kerry, perhaps? It's a contradiction in terms

explanation.definitionFit: Kerry is an Irish breed of cattle, so a Kerry male is one example; the phrase also names a ludicrously self-contradictory statement.

clue.text: Turned up to pick out of whatever's available

definitions.text: Turned up to pick out of whatever's available

parts.words: Turned up to pick out of whatever's available
parts.note: a guest who arrives at a shared meal and takes from whatever dishes others have brought, rather than ordering

explanation.surface: Someone arrives and selects from what happens to be on offer.
explanation.definitionFit: Pot luck is whatever food or chance happens to be available, as at a meal where guests bring dishes.

clue.text: Strong drink

explanation.definitionFit: Stout means sturdy and robust; it is also a dark heavy beer.

clue.text: … put back on the Sabbath, I would appear slow

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece placed on another follows it, so the turned word comes after the Sabbath letter

parts.note: S is a dictionary abbreviation for Sabbath

indicators.note: put back tells us to read the word put in reverse

parts.note: taken as written before being turned round
I would contracts to I'd

explanation.surface: Continuing 1-across, someone delayed until Sunday looks dim-witted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns PUT into TUP, which sits 'on' (after) S; then I'D. The ellipsis links back to 1-across, whose last words reappear here.
explanation.definitionFit: Slow is a common word for dull-witted, unquick at understanding.

clue.text: Other people accept the blame for this treatment

indicators.note: the word for other people takes in, accepts, the word for blame

parts.note: they means people other than ourselves
to take the rap is to take the blame

explanation.surface: Letting others shoulder the fault is presented as a remedy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accept' puts RAP inside THEY; 'for this' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Therapy is treatment meant to heal or relieve a disorder.

clue.text: Fold suit and shirt

parts.note: a plea is a lawsuit or legal claim
T as in T-shirt

explanation.surface: Creasing a jacket and a shirt neatly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suit' looks like clothing; it is a lawsuit.
explanation.definitionFit: A pleat is a fold of cloth pressed or stitched in place.

clue.text: Force Ted to become a turncoat

indicators.note: the letters are forced to become something else, rearranged

explanation.surface: Pressuring a man named Ted into switching sides.
explanation.definitionFit: A defector abandons their side for another, just as a turncoat changes allegiance.

clue.text: City where witches go

parts.note: a coven is a gathering of witches
a go is an attempt, a try

explanation.surface: Where witches head off to.
explanation.walkthrough: COVENTRY is an English city; being 'sent to Coventry' means being shunned.
explanation.definitionFit: Coventry is a city in the English Midlands.

clue.text: Badly off, her son is left to cope alone

indicators.note: badly says the following words are put together wrongly, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A poorly provided woman's boy has been abandoned to manage by himself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Badly' rearranges the fifteen letters of OFF HER SON IS LEFT; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To shift for oneself is an idiom for managing without help from anyone.

clue.text: Wear out a car component

explanation.definitionFit: Exhaust as a verb means tire out completely; as a noun it is the pipe system that carries fumes away from a car's engine.

clue.text: Adaptable feature of the last ice, age

indicators.note: a feature of the phrase is a run of letters found within it

explanation.surface: Flexibility as a characteristic of the most recent glacial period.
explanation.walkthrough: 'feature of' points to a run inside 'thE LAST ICe-age'.
explanation.definitionFit: Elastic means able to stretch or adjust, so flexible or accommodating.

clue.text: The charge when money's stolen

parts.note: bucks is slang for dollars, money; the 's is read as 'is'
hot is slang for stolen goods

explanation.surface: A criminal accusation brought when cash has been taken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charge' looks like an accusation; it is a load fired from a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: A charge is the load in a gun, and shot of the size for deer is a typical shotgun load.

clue.text: Wonderful! Swell! Just nothing missing!

parts.note: to heave is to rise and fall, as the sea swells

indicators.note: missing means the letter for nothing is absent from the word for just

parts.note: only means just, merely
nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: A string of excited exclamations about something perfect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swell' looks like praise; it is HEAVE. 'missing' removes O from ONLY to leave NLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Heavenly is used informally for delightful or superb.

clue.text: See lout dance round — and round — and round

indicators.note: turned round, the word for the dance is read back to front

parts.note: the hay (or hey) is an old country dance in which dancers weave round one another
a round shape is the letter O
another round shape, another letter O

explanation.surface: Watch a hooligan spinning about and about in a dizzy jig.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'round' turns HAY into YAH; the next two each give O. 'See' is a link inviting us to look.
explanation.definitionFit: Yahoo, from Swift's brutish creatures, is a crude, boorish person.

clue.text: It's lucky when animals keep the weeds down

parts.note: horses are animals
to hoe is to chop weeds with a garden tool

explanation.surface: Good fortune follows if livestock graze the weeds short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A horseshoe hung on a door is a traditional good-luck charm.

clue.text: To be successful with a meal is hard

parts.note: meal is coarsely ground grain, like flour
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Thriving with food is tough going.
explanation.definitionFit: To flourish is to thrive and prosper.

clue.text: Without iodine, ring turns purple

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the turned word goes round the iodine symbol
the word for ring turns, reading backwards

parts.note: to ring someone is to call them
I is the chemical symbol for iodine

explanation.surface: Lacking an element, a hoop changes colour in a chemistry demonstration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks like 'lacking', but means outside: 'turns' makes LLAC from CALL, which goes round I.
explanation.definitionFit: Lilac is a pale purple colour, named after the flowering shrub.

clue.text: Two beverages, you said, obtainable from this vineyard

parts.note: cha is a slang word for tea
tea, the drink itself

indicators.note: said means the word you is spoken, giving its sound as one letter

parts.note: taken as written for its sound

explanation.surface: Two drinks, you mention, are available at this wine estate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'obtainable from this' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A chateau is a French wine estate, a winery with its vineyard.

clue.text: Why are leaderless men regrouping in no particular place?

indicators.note: regrouping says the letters are gathered into a fresh order
the leader of the word men, its first letter, is removed

explanation.surface: Asking why soldiers without a commander are reforming at some unspecified spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaderless' turns MEN into EN; 'regrouping' rearranges WHY ARE EN.
explanation.definitionFit: Anywhere means at any place at all, wherever, without a specific location.

clue.text: Ben — he's a strange old fogy

indicators.note: strange suggests the letters are in an odd, altered order

explanation.surface: Remarking that Ben is an eccentric, out-of-touch old man.
explanation.definitionFit: A has-been is a person whose best days are past, out of date like an old fogy.

clue.text: Committed to memory a play and several books

parts.note: King Lear is a play by Shakespeare
NT is the New Testament, a collection of books

explanation.surface: Memorising a drama and a number of volumes.
explanation.definitionFit: Learnt means memorised, fixed in the mind.

clue.text: Draw attention from the London-bound coach?

parts.note: travelling to London is going up in British railway usage
a stage, or stagecoach, is a horse-drawn coach

explanation.surface: Stealing the limelight from a capital-bound bus.
explanation.walkthrough: Trains to London are 'up' trains in Britain. A STAGE is a stagecoach.
explanation.definitionFit: To upstage an actor is to take the audience's focus away from them, originally by moving upstage.

clue.text: Take industrial action, but go the wrong way about it

indicators.note: the word for doing wrong goes about the word it

parts.note: to sin is to stray from the right path
taken as written

explanation.surface: Advice to strike, but in a misguided fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go the wrong way' looks like a comment on tactics but means SIN, a verb, around IT; 'but' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A sit-in is a protest in which workers occupy their workplace.

clue.text: It's grave in the latter stages from 11-20

indicators.note: only the later portions of the two named answers are kept, their opening parts dropped

parts.note: the numbers refer to the answers at 11-across and 20-across
the numbers refer to the answers at 11-across and 20-across

explanation.surface: A tombstone lies further along a route between two points.
explanation.walkthrough: From the answers to 11 and 20, keep only the closing portions, AUST and ERE. 'It's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Grave and austere both describe a stern, serious, unsmiling manner.

clue.text: It sounds like an African affair

indicators.note: sounds like tells us the answer is said the same as the phrase for an African

parts.note: a Moor is a North African

explanation.surface: Something that seems like a romance in Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: A Moor was a North African of Arab and Berber descent; 'It' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An amour is a love affair, often a secret one.

clue.text: I am exposed — I am thine, besotted completely

indicators.note: besotted, as if drunk, says the letters of thine reel into new positions

parts.note: altogether means completely

explanation.surface: A lover confesses vulnerability and declares utter, infatuated devotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'besotted' rearranges THINE to IN THE; the two uses of 'I am' frame the clue as 'I am naked' and are links.
explanation.definitionFit: In the altogether is an idiom for naked, with nothing on, so uncovered.

clue.text: Ended the conversation in a state of anxiety

explanation.definitionFit: To hang up is to end a phone call by replacing the receiver; hung up as slang means worried or neurotic.

clue.text: Wing producing patterns in motion

indicators.note: in motion means the letters are moving about into a new order

explanation.surface: A bird's wing beating to create shapes as it flies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wing' suggests a bird or plane; it is part of a church.
explanation.definitionFit: A transept is either arm crossing the nave of a cross-shaped church, a side wing of the building.
